main_text.l: ñem confumit. Paulus Ægineta libro de re
Medica quarto, & Actuarius fecundo Me-
thodi medédi, utrunq; affectum perfpicuè
discernunt. Nam qui à fæce fanguinis origi-
nem habet, is in principio fubruber eft, &
mitior quodammodo, qui tàdem in nigro-
rem conuertitur: alter, qui à bile adusta na-
scitur malignior est, & totum corpus exul-
cerat, extremasque partes decidere facit.
His addit Actuarius fuperciliorum menti-
qúe pilorum defluuia affectum præcedere,
& tumores in facie extuberates, oculosq;
alio & alio colore notari, ac uocem exafpe
rari:uenas item fub lingua turgidas, & quæ
antea huiusmodi non essent, nigras efficiunt.
Quòd uerò ad ætatem pertinet, pueros cū
hoc morbo non conflictari, donec pubesce-
re incipiant satis docet experientia. Regio
autem huic malo opportuna ea eft, quæ uel
percalida eft, uel supra modum frigida, eò
quòd hæc fanguinem incrasset, refrigeret-
que, perspirationes prohibeat, ac denique
insitum calorem opprimat: illa uerò, quòd
ipsum sanguinem adasset. Propterea Gale-
nus libro ad Glauconem secundo ait pluri
mos in Alexandria ob crassam victus ratio-
nem, atq; regionis feruorem elephantiasi
corripi:

page.notes: The first word "ñem" is a fragment with a tilde over the n, kept as printed. The catchword "P" stands alone on the line after "elephantiasi" at the left, under the text; it is probably a printer's mark or catchword and is doubtful. The reading "fubruber" and "perfpicuè" are as printed. The word "tàdem" has a grave accent as printed. The ligature in "Actuarius" and the long s in "fuperciliorum" and "fecundo" are transcribed with plain s.
